# Charts cookbook

Each spec below renders as-is with `charts_render` and the rows shown passed as `data.rows` (generated from the plugin's own catalogue; `charts_catalogue {"id": "…"}` returns any of them with full data). Colours written `"theme:…"` follow the active theme. Vega-Lite is the default engine; Vega is for layouts (treemap, sunburst, tree, force, word cloud); ECharts for flows and dashboard types (Sankey, chord, gauge, funnel, calendar, candlestick, radar, parallel).

## comparison

### Bar chart — `bar` (vega-lite)

Compare a value across a few categories. **Avoid:** Over ~15 categories: use horizontal_bar.

Rows like: `[{"product":"Lattes","revenue_eur":182400},{"product":"Pastries","revenue_eur":96300}]`

```json
{"mark":"bar","encoding":{"x":{"field":"product","type":"nominal","sort":"-y"},"y":{"field":"revenue_eur","type":"quantitative"}}}
```

### Horizontal bar (ranked) — `horizontal_bar` (vega-lite)

Rank many categories, or long category names.

Rows like: `[{"country":"Germany","users_k":820},{"country":"France","users_k":796}]`

```json
{"mark":"bar","encoding":{"y":{"field":"country","type":"nominal","sort":"-x"},"x":{"field":"users_k","type":"quantitative"}}}
```

### Grouped bar — `grouped_bar` (vega-lite)

Compare sub-groups side by side within each category (xOffset). **Avoid:** More than ~4 sub-groups: use small multiples.

Rows like: `[{"region":"North","quarter":"Q1","revenue_eur":400000},{"region":"North","quarter":"Q2","revenue_eur":535000}]`

```json
{"mark":"bar","encoding":{"x":{"field":"region","type":"nominal"},"xOffset":{"field":"quarter"},"y":{"field":"revenue_eur","type":"quantitative"},"color":{"field":"quarter","type":"nominal"}}}
```

### Stacked bar — `stacked_bar` (vega-lite)

Show totals and their make-up across categories or time.

Rows like: `[{"date":"2024-01-01","series":"Web","orders":1200},{"date":"2024-02-01","series":"Web","orders":1374.7}]`

```json
{"mark":"bar","encoding":{"x":{"field":"date","type":"ordinal","timeUnit":"yearmonth","title":"Month"},"y":{"aggregate":"sum","field":"orders","type":"quantitative","title":"Orders"},"color":{"field":"series","type":"nominal","title":"Channel"}}}
```

### Diverging bar — `diverging_bar` (vega-lite)

Gains and losses around zero.

Rows like: `[{"country":"Germany","change_pct":-0.12},{"country":"France","change_pct":-0.06}]`

```json
{"mark":"bar","encoding":{"y":{"field":"country","type":"nominal","sort":"-x"},"x":{"field":"change_pct","type":"quantitative","axis":{"format":"+.0%"},"title":"Change vs 2023"},"color":{"condition":{"test":"datum.change_pct < 0","value":"theme:negative"},"value":"theme:positive"}}}
```

### Lollipop — `lollipop` (vega-lite)

A lighter bar chart for many categories.

Rows like: `[{"store":"Germany","nps":18},{"store":"France","nps":41}]`

```json
{"encoding":{"y":{"field":"store","type":"nominal","sort":"-x"},"x":{"field":"nps","type":"quantitative","title":"NPS (points)"}},"layer":[{"mark":{"type":"rule","strokeWidth":2,"color":"theme:axis"},"encoding":{"x":{"datum":0},"x2":{"field":"nps"}}},{"mark":{"type":"point","filled":true,"size":120}}]}
```

### Dumbbell — `dumbbell` (vega-lite)

Before/after or two values per category.

Rows like: `[{"area":"Search","when":"Before","score":52},{"area":"Search","when":"After","score":61}]`

```json
{"encoding":{"y":{"field":"area","type":"nominal"},"x":{"field":"score","type":"quantitative","scale":{"zero":false},"title":"Score (0–100)"}},"layer":[{"mark":{"type":"line","color":"theme:axis","strokeWidth":2},"encoding":{"detail":{"field":"area"}}},{"mark":{"type":"point","filled":true,"size":110,"opacity":1},"encoding":{"color":{"field":"when","type":"nominal","sort":["Before","After"],"title":null}}}]}
```

### Dot plot (Cleveland) — `dot_plot` (vega-lite)

Precise comparison when bars would be heavy; non-zero baselines are fine.

Rows like: `[{"city":"Berlin","delivery_min":24},{"city":"Paris","delivery_min":41}]`

```json
{"mark":{"type":"point","filled":true,"size":90},"encoding":{"y":{"field":"city","type":"nominal","sort":"x"},"x":{"field":"delivery_min","type":"quantitative","scale":{"zero":false},"title":"Median delivery (min)"}}}
```

### Bullet chart — `bullet` (vega-lite)

Actual against target with qualitative bands (KPIs).

Rows like: `[{"kpi":"Revenue (€k)","poor":600,"ok":800,"good":1000,"actual":870,"target":900},{"kpi":"New customers","poor":300,"ok":450,"good":600,"actual":510,"target":480}]`


## part-to-whole

### 100% stacked bar — `normalized_bar` (vega-lite)

Compare shares (not totals) across categories.

Rows like: `[{"region":"North","channel":"Web","orders":400},{"region":"North","channel":"App","orders":535}]`

```json
{"mark":"bar","encoding":{"y":{"field":"region","type":"nominal"},"x":{"aggregate":"sum","field":"orders","type":"quantitative","stack":"normalize","axis":{"format":".0%"},"title":"Share of orders"},"color":{"field":"channel","type":"nominal"}}}
```

### Pie chart — `pie` (vega-lite)

Parts of one whole, 2–5 slices. **Avoid:** More than 5–7 slices, or comparing pies: use bars.

Rows like: `[{"source":"Search","visits":4200},{"source":"Direct","visits":2600}]`

```json
{"mark":{"type":"arc"},"encoding":{"theta":{"field":"visits","type":"quantitative","stack":true},"color":{"field":"source","type":"nominal","sort":{"field":"visits","order":"descending"}},"order":{"field":"visits","sort":"descending"}}}
```

### Donut chart — `donut` (vega-lite)

A pie with room for a total in the middle.

Rows like: `[{"item":"Payroll","share":0.52},{"item":"Infrastructure","share":0.21}]`

```json
{"layer":[{"mark":{"type":"arc","innerRadius":70,"padAngle":0.01},"encoding":{"theta":{"field":"share","type":"quantitative","stack":true},"color":{"field":"item","type":"nominal","sort":null},"order":{"field":"share","sort":"descending"}}},{"data":{"values":[{}]},"mark":{"type":"text","fontSize":22,"fontWeight":500},"encoding":{"text":{"value":"€4.2M"}}}]}
```

### Radial (rose) chart — `radial` (vega-lite)

Cyclical categories such as months or directions.

Rows like: `[{"month":"Jan","rain_mm":75},{"month":"Feb","rain_mm":76}]`

```json
{"mark":{"type":"arc","stroke":"theme:background","strokeWidth":1},"encoding":{"theta":{"field":"month","type":"nominal","sort":null},"radius":{"field":"rain_mm","type":"quantitative","scale":{"type":"sqrt","zero":true,"rangeMin":20}},"color":{"field":"rain_mm","type":"quantitative","legend":null}}}
```

### Funnel — `funnel` (echarts)

Drop-off through ordered stages.

```json
{"series":[{"type":"funnel","left":"10%","width":"80%","sort":"descending","gap":2,"label":{"show":true,"position":"inside","formatter":"{b}  {c}"},"data":[{"name":"Visited","value":10000},{"name":"Viewed product","value":6200},{"name":"Added to basket","value":2400},{"name":"Checkout","value":1300},{"name":"Paid","value":980}]}]}
```

### Gauge — `gauge` (echarts)

One KPI against its range, for dashboards. **Avoid:** Several KPIs: use bullet charts.

```json
{"series":[{"type":"gauge","min":99,"max":100,"startAngle":210,"endAngle":-30,"progress":{"show":true,"width":14},"axisLine":{"lineStyle":{"width":14}},"pointer":{"show":false},"axisTick":{"show":false},"splitLine":{"show":false},"axisLabel":{"distance":20,"fontSize":10},"detail":{"formatter":"{value}%","fontSize":30,"offsetCenter":[0,"10%"]},"title":{"offsetCenter":[0,"38%"]},"data":[{"value":99.94,"name":"Uptime"}]}]}
```

## trend

### Line chart — `line` (vega-lite)

A value over time.

Rows like: `[{"date":"2024-01-01","dau":42000},{"date":"2024-02-01","dau":45854}]`

```json
{"mark":{"type":"line","point":true},"encoding":{"x":{"field":"date","type":"temporal","title":null},"y":{"field":"dau","type":"quantitative","title":"Daily active users"}}}
```

### Multi-series line — `multi_line` (vega-lite)

Compare a few series over time (≤ 7). **Avoid:** More than ~7 series: highlight one or use small multiples.

Rows like: `[{"date":"2024-01-01","series":"Search","conversion_rate":0},{"date":"2024-02-01","series":"Search","conversion_rate":0}]`

```json
{"mark":"line","encoding":{"x":{"field":"date","type":"temporal","title":null},"y":{"field":"conversion_rate","type":"quantitative","axis":{"format":".1%"},"title":"Conversion rate"},"color":{"field":"series","type":"nominal","title":"Channel"}}}
```

### Area chart — `area` (vega-lite)

A single volume over time.

Rows like: `[{"date":"2024-01-01","storage_tb":40},{"date":"2024-02-01","storage_tb":48}]`

```json
{"mark":{"type":"area","line":true},"encoding":{"x":{"field":"date","type":"temporal","title":null},"y":{"field":"storage_tb","type":"quantitative"}}}
```

### Stacked area — `stacked_area` (vega-lite)

Totals over time and how parts contribute.

Rows like: `[{"date":"2024-01-01","region":"North","revenue_eur":300000},{"date":"2024-02-01","region":"North","revenue_eur":336141}]`

```json
{"mark":"area","encoding":{"x":{"field":"date","type":"temporal","title":null},"y":{"field":"revenue_eur","type":"quantitative","stack":"zero"},"color":{"field":"region","type":"nominal"}}}
```

### Streamgraph — `streamgraph` (vega-lite)

Changing composition where the overall shape matters more than exact values.

Rows like: `[{"date":"2024-01-01","genre":"Pop","hours":200},{"date":"2024-02-01","genre":"Pop","hours":244}]`

```json
{"mark":"area","encoding":{"x":{"field":"date","type":"temporal","title":null,"axis":{"domain":false,"grid":false}},"y":{"aggregate":"sum","field":"hours","type":"quantitative","stack":"center","axis":null},"color":{"field":"genre","type":"nominal"}}}
```

### Step line — `step_line` (vega-lite)

Values that change at discrete moments (prices, rates, plans).

Rows like: `[{"date":"2024-01-01","rate":0.045},{"date":"2024-02-01","rate":0.045}]`

```json
{"mark":{"type":"line","interpolate":"step-after"},"encoding":{"x":{"field":"date","type":"temporal","title":null},"y":{"field":"rate","type":"quantitative","axis":{"format":".2%"},"scale":{"zero":false},"title":"Rate"}}}
```

### Line with confidence band — `line_band` (vega-lite)

An estimate with its uncertainty.

Rows like: `[{"date":"2024-01-01","forecast":500,"low":470,"high":530},{"date":"2024-02-01","forecast":550.2,"low":514.2,"high":586.2}]`

```json
{"encoding":{"x":{"field":"date","type":"temporal","title":null}},"layer":[{"mark":{"type":"area","opacity":0.25},"encoding":{"y":{"field":"low","type":"quantitative","title":"Units per day"},"y2":{"field":"high"}}},{"mark":"line","encoding":{"y":{"field":"forecast","type":"quantitative"}}}]}
```

### Slope chart — `slope` (vega-lite)

Change between two moments for several items.

Rows like: `[{"brand":"Alpha","year":"2023","share":0.31},{"brand":"Alpha","year":"2024","share":0.27}]`

```json
{"encoding":{"x":{"field":"year","type":"ordinal","axis":{"labelAngle":0},"title":null},"y":{"field":"share","type":"quantitative","axis":{"format":".0%"},"title":"Market share"},"color":{"field":"brand","type":"nominal","legend":null}},"layer":[{"mark":{"type":"line","point":true}},{"mark":{"type":"text","align":"left","dx":8},"encoding":{"text":{"field":"brand"}},"transform":[{"filter":"datum.year === '2024'"}]}]}
```

### Bump chart — `bump` (vega-lite)

Rank changes over time.

Rows like: `[{"week":1,"team":"Lions","rank":4},{"week":2,"team":"Lions","rank":3}]`

```json
{"mark":{"type":"line","point":{"size":80,"filled":true},"interpolate":"monotone"},"encoding":{"x":{"field":"week","type":"ordinal","title":"Week"},"y":{"field":"rank","type":"ordinal","title":"Position"},"color":{"field":"team","type":"nominal"}}}
```

### Dual axis (bar + line) — `dual_axis` (vega-lite)

Two measures with different units that share time — label both axes. **Avoid:** Readers compare heights across axes; prefer two aligned charts.

Rows like: `[{"date":"2024-01-01","orders":3200,"basket_eur":41.6},{"date":"2024-02-01","orders":3515,"basket_eur":41.1}]`

```json
{"encoding":{"x":{"field":"date","type":"temporal","timeUnit":"yearmonth","title":null}},"layer":[{"mark":{"type":"bar","opacity":0.8},"encoding":{"y":{"field":"orders","type":"quantitative","title":"Orders"}}},{"mark":{"type":"line","color":"theme:categorical.1","strokeWidth":3},"encoding":{"y":{"field":"basket_eur","type":"quantitative","title":"Average basket (€)","axis":{"titleColor":"theme:categorical.1"}}}}],"resolve":{"scale":{"y":"independent"}}}
```

### Small multiples (facet) — `small_multiples` (vega-lite)

Many series: one small chart each, same scales.

Rows like: `[{"date":"2024-01-01","region":"North","signups":900},{"date":"2024-02-01","region":"North","signups":1019}]`

```json
{"facet":{"field":"region","type":"nominal","title":null},"columns":2,"spec":{"width":240,"height":120,"mark":"area","encoding":{"x":{"field":"date","type":"temporal","title":null,"axis":{"format":"%b"}},"y":{"field":"signups","type":"quantitative","title":"Sign-ups"}}}}
```

### Calendar heatmap — `calendar_heatmap` (echarts)

Daily values over a year, where weekday patterns matter.

Rows like: `[{"date":"2024-01-01","commits":3},{"date":"2024-01-02","commits":5}]`

```json
{"visualMap":{"min":0,"max":14,"orient":"horizontal","left":"center","bottom":4,"itemHeight":120,"calculable":false},"calendar":{"range":"2024","cellSize":["auto",14],"left":64,"right":24},"series":[{"type":"heatmap","coordinateSystem":"calendar","encode":{"time":"date","value":"commits"}}]}
```

### Candlestick — `candlestick` (echarts)

Open, high, low and close per period.

Rows like: `[{"date":"2024-03-01","open":100,"close":102.5,"low":98.8,"high":103.6},{"date":"2024-03-02","open":104.75,"close":103.43,"low":101.83,"high":106.15}]`

```json
{"xAxis":{"type":"category","axisLabel":{"interval":4}},"yAxis":{"type":"value","scale":true,"name":"€"},"series":[{"type":"candlestick","encode":{"x":"date","y":["open","close","low","high"]}}]}
```

## map

### World choropleth — `choropleth_world` (vega-lite)

A rate by country. Join on iso_a3, iso_a2 or name from the bundled world-110m atlas. **Avoid:** Totals (bigger countries dominate): map rates, or use a bubble map.

Rows like: `[{"iso":"USA","users_share":0.92},{"iso":"CAN","users_share":0.93}]`

```json
{"data":{"atlas":"world-110m"},"projection":{"type":"equalEarth"},"transform":[{"lookup":"properties.iso_a3","from":{"data":{"name":"table"},"key":"iso","fields":["users_share"]}}],"mark":{"type":"geoshape"},"encoding":{"color":{"field":"users_share","type":"quantitative","legend":{"format":".0%"},"title":"Internet users","condition":{"test":"datum.users_share == null","value":"theme:grid"}}}}
```

### US states choropleth — `choropleth_us` (vega-lite)

A rate by US state (join on postal, name or FIPS id).

Rows like: `[{"postal":"CA","unemployment":0.025},{"postal":"TX","unemployment":0.032}]`

```json
{"data":{"atlas":"us-states-10m"},"projection":{"type":"albersUsa"},"transform":[{"lookup":"properties.postal","from":{"data":{"name":"table"},"key":"postal","fields":["unemployment"]}}],"mark":"geoshape","encoding":{"color":{"field":"unemployment","type":"quantitative","legend":{"format":".1%"},"title":"Unemployment"}}}
```

# Charts

## Which way to draw

| Use the charts_* tools when | Use code on the machine (Python: matplotlib, seaborn, plotly, pandas) when |
|---|---|
| The chart is a standard type (bar, line, scatter, map, Sankey, treemap… see `charts_catalogue`). | The chart is bespoke analysis output: a statistical model's diagnostics, a custom annotation-heavy figure, anything the catalogue cannot express. |
| It must match a theme or brand exactly, and look the same every time. | The data needs heavy processing first and the plot is a by-product of that script. |
| You want it checked: field names, misleading axes, overlapping labels. | You need a library feature (3-D, scientific projections, image overlays). |

Both end the same way: a file under `outputs/` that the person can open. Prefer the tools: they are deterministic, themed, checked and fast.

## Workflow

1. **Pick the type.** `charts_catalogue` lists every type with when to use it; `charts_catalogue {"id": "…"}` gives a working call to adapt. For a basic chart, `charts_quick` builds the spec from field names.
2. **Pass data separately**: `data.rows` (inline) or `data.path` (a workspace CSV, TSV, JSON, JSONL or Parquet file). Reshape with `data.transform` (Vega-Lite transforms: `filter`, `calculate`, `aggregate`, `window`, `pivot`, `fold`) rather than by hand. In the spec, refer to the rows as `{"name": "table"}` or leave `data` out.
3. **Check, then render.** `charts_validate` returns every problem with its JSON path and a fix ("Field "regoin" is not in the data. Did you mean "region"?"), lint warnings, layout facts and the picture. Fix, then `charts_render`.
4. **Look at it.** The result includes the PNG when there are warnings (or with `inspect: true`). Fix every warning that is real: overlapping labels, clipped text, a pie with too many slices, a bar axis that does not start at zero, missing units.
5. **Show it**: put the returned markdown line (`![title](outputs/charts/name.png)`) in your reply. To hand files over, save them with the host's file-saving tool (in Jelly: `jelly_file_save` with the path); files under `outputs/` are also kept when the turn ends. Ask for `formats: ["svg","png","html"]` when the person wants an interactive version.

## Getting it right first time

- One message per chart. A title that states the finding ("Revenue doubled in Q3"), not the variables.
- Units on every quantitative axis: `"title": "Revenue (€k)"`. Field names like `revenue_eur` are humanised to "Revenue (€)" automatically.
- Money: pass `currency: "EUR"` (and `locale: "de-DE"` for German separators). Large numbers are shown compactly (1.2M) automatically.
- Time on x as `"type": "temporal"` with ISO dates (`2024-03-01`). Everything is UTC, so output is the same on every machine.
- Order categories by value (`"sort": "-y"`), except natural orders (months and weekdays are ordered for you).
- Colour: use the theme. Refer to theme colours as `"theme:positive"`, `"theme:negative"`, `"theme:highlight"`, `"theme:categorical.2"`. Sequential data gets the theme's sequential ramp; never a rainbow.
- Maps: `{"atlas": "world-110m"}` (join on `properties.iso_a3`, `iso_a2` or `name`), `us-states-10m` (join on `properties.postal`), `world-land-110m` (base map). Nothing loads from the network; URLs are refused.
- Pie or donut only for 2–5 parts of one whole; otherwise bars.

## Themes

Built in: `light` (default), `dark`, `high-contrast`, `print`, `presentation`, `toqan`, `toqan-night`. A brand: `charts_theme_save {"name": "acme", "theme": {"extends": "light", "colors": {"categorical": ["#…", …]}, "font": {"family": "Geist"}}}`, then `theme: "acme"` everywhere. `charts_themes {"name": "light"}` shows every token to copy. Bundled fonts: Inter, Geist, JetBrains Mono; a theme can add workspace `.ttf` files with `font.files`.

# opencode-charts

Unofficial OpenCode plugin: deterministic, themed charts from a spec. It takes Vega-Lite, Vega or ECharts in, and
writes SVG, PNG (1–3x) and an optional offline interactive HTML page under `outputs/charts/`. The same input gives
the same bytes on the same platform, and the same picture on any: across platforms a coordinate can differ only in
its last digits. Nothing is ever loaded from the network.

- **Any chart.** 53 tested chart types:
  - statistical charts, facets, layers, dual axes and selections (Vega-Lite);
  - treemap, sunburst, tree, force network and word cloud (Vega);
  - Sankey, chord, gauge, funnel, calendar heatmap, candlestick, radar and parallel coordinates (ECharts);
  - world and US maps from bundled atlases.
- **Any theme.** `light`, `dark`, `high-contrast`, `print`, `presentation`, `toqan` and `toqan-night`, or your own tokens, saved by name. Palettes are colour-blind-safe and checked for contrast. Fonts are bundled (Inter, Geist, JetBrains Mono), so text measures and draws identically everywhere.
- **Right first time.**
  - Validation that teaches: `Field "revenu" is not in the data. Did you mean "revenue"?`, with the JSON path.
  - Lint for misleading or unreadable charts.
  - Overlap and clipping checks on the drawn chart.
  - The rendered PNG returned for the model to look at.
- **Safe.** No URLs, loaders or images. Workspace-confined paths, size and expression caps, and a worker with a time and memory limit.

## Install

```json
{ "plugin": ["@joe-broadhead/opencode-charts@0.0.2"] }
```

Options (all optional):

```json
{ "plugin": [["@joe-broadhead/opencode-charts@0.0.2", { "theme": "light", "locale": "en-GB", "outDir": "outputs/charts", "themes": { "acme": { "extends": "light", "colors": { "categorical": ["#0B5FFF", "#FF6A3D", "#00A87E"] } } } }]] }
```

The host range is `>=2.2.5 <2.3.0`. Options, permissions, limits and errors are in
[docs/configuration.md](docs/configuration.md).

## Permissions

The three tools that write files (`charts_render`, `charts_quick`, `charts_theme_save`) ask before they run, and the
three that only read run without asking: the plugin puts that default block after each agent's base allow rule, and
your own `permissions` can change it. Each tool also asks for `read` on a data file and `edit` on its output folder.

## Status

`/charts-status` shows the renderers, the defaults, the themes, the skills, the tools the agent can see, any agent
that would run the writers without asking, the OpenCode version and the next step.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `charts_render` | Any spec (Vega-Lite, Vega or ECharts, detected) plus `data` (`rows`, or a workspace `path` to CSV, TSV, JSON, JSONL or Parquet, with optional Vega-Lite `transform`s). Writes `<name>.svg`, `<name>.png` and `<name>.vl.json` (plus `.html` on request), and returns a markdown image line to show it inline. |
| `charts_quick` | `bar`, `horizontal_bar`, `grouped_bar`, `stacked_bar`, `line`, `area`, `stacked_area`, `scatter`, `bubble`, `pie`, `donut`, `histogram`, `box_plot` and `heatmap`, from field names. |
| `charts_validate` | The same checks as render, plus the PNG, with no files written. |
| `charts_catalogue` | Every chart type, and a working example of any. |
| `charts_themes` / `charts_theme_save` | List themes and their tokens; save a brand theme to `.charts/themes/<name>.json`. |

Example:

```json
{
  "spec": { "mark": "bar", "encoding": { "x": { "field": "region", "type": "nominal", "sort": "-y" }, "y": { "field": "revenue_eur", "type": "quantitative" } } },
  "data": { "path": "data/sales.csv" },
  "title": "Revenue by region, 2024",
  "theme": "toqan",
  "currency": "EUR",
  "locale": "de-DE"
}
```

In a spec, refer to the data as `{"name": "table"}` (or leave `data` out), to maps as `{"atlas": "world-110m"}`,
`"us-states-10m"` or `"world-land-110m"`, and to theme colours as `"theme:positive"`, `"theme:categorical.2"` and so on.
